1. // Spec helpers for `FrameAddress` are shared with the `phys` sibling module: a frame's abstract
2. // state is the physical address (`int`), its frame number is `self@ / spec_page_size()`, and its
3. // base address is `frame_index * spec_page_size()`.
4. use crate::hal::mem::types::address::phys::{
5.     spec_frame_number,
6.     spec_from_number,
7.     spec_frame_raw_value,
8.     spec_max_frame_number,
9. };
10. 
11. // The former `assume_specification` for `<PhysicalAddress as ::sys::mm::Address>::from_raw_value`
12. // was removed: it supplied a trusted, unverified contract to a kernel-internal (intra-crate)
13. // callee that is not sanctioned in `tcb-allowed.md`. Its sole consumer, `FrameAddress::from_raw_value`,
14. // is instead carried as a TCB-listed `#[verus_verify(external_body)]` (see `frame.rs`), so no
15. // intra-crate trust hole remains here.
16.

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. //==================================================================================================
5. // Imports
6. //==================================================================================================
7. 
8. use vstd::prelude::*;
9. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
10. include!("frame.spec.rs");
11. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
12. include!("frame.proof.rs");
13. 
14. use crate::hal::mem::types::address::{
15.     Address,
16.     PageAddress,
17.     PageAligned,
18.     PhysicalAddress,
19. };
20. use ::arch::mem::paging::FrameNumber;
21. use ::sys::error::Error;
22. 
23. //==================================================================================================
24. // Structures
25. //==================================================================================================
26. 
27. ///
28. /// # Description
29. ///
30. /// A type that represents a frame address.
31. ///
32. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
33. #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
34. pub struct FrameAddress(PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>);
35. 
36. #[cfg(verus_keep_ghost)]
37. verus! {
38. 
39. // The architectural page size, delegating to the `arch` crate's verified `PAGE_SIZE` constant.
40. // Formerly an `uninterp spec fn` paired with a placeholder `assume_specification[PAGE_SIZE]`; now
41. // that `arch` carries a real verified spec for `PAGE_SIZE`, that placeholder is superseded and this
42. // definition names the same concrete value the proofs already relied on.
43. pub open spec fn spec_page_size() -> int {
44.     ::arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE as int
45. }
46. 
47. impl View for FrameAddress
48. {
49.     type V = int;
50. 
51.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int
52.     {
53.         self.0@
54.     }
55. }
56. 
57. impl FrameAddress {
58.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool
59.     {
60.         self@ % spec_page_size() == 0
61.     }
62. }
63. 
64. }
65. 
66. //==================================================================================================
67. // Implementations
68. //==================================================================================================
69. 
70. impl FrameAddress {
71.     pub fn new(address: PageAligned<PhysicalAddress>) -> Self {
72.         Self(address)
73.     }
74. 
75.     pub fn into_physical_address(self) -> PageAligned<PhysicalAddress> {
76.         self.0
77.     }
78. 
79.     pub fn into_page_address(self) -> PageAddress {
80.         PageAddress::new(PageAligned::into_virtual_address(self.0))
81.     }
82. }
83. 
84. // Raw-value and frame-number conversions of a frame address. The frame address denotes a single
85. // page-aligned physical frame; these functions expose its two equivalent identities (raw physical
86. // address and frame number) and the lossless, mutually-inverse mappings between them.
87. #[verus_verify]
88. impl FrameAddress {
89.     // Succeeds only for page-aligned inputs, so the resulting frame address satisfies `inv()` and
90.     // its abstract address equals the raw input. `external_body` (TCB-sanctioned per
91.     // `tcb-allowed.md`) until the intra-crate `PhysicalAddress` `Address` impl carries its own
92.     // verified `#[verus_spec]`; the strengthened contract below is preserved verbatim so callers
93.     // keep the full `fa@ == raw_addr` guarantee.
94.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
95.     #[verus_spec(result =>
96.         ensures
97.             match result {
98.                 Ok(fa) => fa.inv() && fa@ == raw_addr as int,
99.                 Err(_) => true,
100.             },
101.     )]
102.     pub fn from_raw_value(raw_addr: usize) -> Result<Self, Error> {
103.         Ok(Self(PageAligned::from_address(PhysicalAddress::from_raw_value(raw_addr)?)?))
104.     }
105. 
106.     ///
107.     /// # Description
108.     ///
109.     /// Converts a [`FrameAddress`] into a raw value.
110.     ///
111.     /// # Returns
112.     ///
113.     /// The raw value of the target [`FrameAddress`].
114.     ///
115.     // Dependency contract: the raw value is the abstract frame address. Verified against the
116.     // `PageAligned::into_raw_value` dependency contract.
117.     #[verus_spec(result =>
118.         ensures
119.             result as int == self@,
120.     )]
121.     pub fn into_raw_value(self) -> usize {
122.         self.0.into_raw_value()
123.     }
124. 
125.     // Constructs a frame address from a frame number. The frame's base address is
126.     // `frame_number * PAGE_SIZE`, page-aligned by construction, so the call always succeeds and the
127.     // result satisfies `inv()`.
128.     #[verus_spec(result =>
129.         ensures
130.             result is Ok,
131.             (result->Ok_0).inv(),
132.             (result->Ok_0)@ == spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame_number)),
133.     )]
134.     pub fn from_frame_number(frame_number: FrameNumber) -> Result<Self, Error> {
135.         proof! { lemma_frame_base_aligned(frame_number); }
136.         Ok(Self(PageAligned::from_address(PhysicalAddress::from_number(frame_number))?))
137.     }
138. 
139.     // Recovers the frame number of a frame address (`self@ / PAGE_SIZE`). Requires the address to
140.     // be page-aligned and to have a representable frame number (so the underlying conversion does
141.     // not overflow); the result is the exact inverse of `from_frame_number`.
142.     #[verus_spec(result =>
143.         requires
144.             self.inv(),
145.             spec_frame_number(self@) <= spec_max_frame_number(),
146.         ensures
147.             spec_frame_raw_value(result) == spec_frame_number(self@),
148.             spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(result)) == self@,
149.     )]
150.     pub fn into_frame_number(self) -> FrameNumber {
151.         proof! { lemma_aligned_div_mul(self@); }
152.         self.0.into_frame_number()
153.     }
154. }
155. 
156. impl core::fmt::Debug for FrameAddress {
157.     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter) -> core::fmt::Result {
158.         write!(f, "FrameAddress({:#010x})", self.into_raw_value())
159.     }
160. }
161. 
162. impl PartialEq for FrameAddress {
163.     fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
164.         self.0 == other.0
165.     }
166. }
167.

1. use vstd::arithmetic::div_mod::{
2.     lemma_fundamental_div_mod,
3.     lemma_mod_multiples_basic,
4. };
5. 
6. verus! {
7. 
8. // =================================================================================================
9. // Proof obligations for `FrameAddress`'s frame-number conversions.
10. //
11. // The facts below are elementary divisibility properties of `spec_page_size()`, which is the
12. // `#[verus_verify]` constant `arch::mem::PAGE_SIZE == 4096` and therefore strictly positive.
13. // =================================================================================================
14. 
15. // `frame_index * PAGE_SIZE` is a multiple of `PAGE_SIZE`, hence page-aligned. Used by
16. // `from_frame_number` to discharge `PageAligned::from_address`'s alignment success condition.
17. pub proof fn lemma_frame_base_aligned(frame: FrameNumber)
18.     ensures
19.         spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame)) % spec_page_size() == 0,
20. {
21.     // `spec_page_size()` is the transparent constant `PAGE_SIZE == 4096 > 0`.
22.     assert(spec_page_size() == 4096);
23.     // `spec_from_number(spec_frame_raw_value(frame)) == frame@ * spec_page_size()`, a multiple of
24.     // `spec_page_size()`, so its remainder mod `spec_page_size()` is zero.
25.     lemma_mod_multiples_basic(spec_frame_raw_value(frame), spec_page_size());
26. }
27. 
28. // For a page-aligned address, dividing by `PAGE_SIZE` then multiplying recovers the address
29. // exactly. Used by `into_frame_number` to relate the recovered frame number back to `self@`.
30. pub proof fn lemma_aligned_div_mul(addr: int)
31.     requires
32.         addr % spec_page_size() == 0,
33.     ensures
34.         spec_from_number(spec_frame_number(addr)) == addr,
35. {
36.     // `spec_page_size()` is the transparent constant `PAGE_SIZE == 4096 > 0`.
37.     assert(spec_page_size() == 4096);
38.     // `addr == s * (addr / s) + (addr % s)` with `addr % s == 0`, so `(addr / s) * s == addr`.
39.     lemma_fundamental_div_mod(addr, spec_page_size());
40. }
41. 
42. } // verus!
43.
